meta.title: Historicity of the Qur'an vs the Bible
meta.thesis: Which scripture has the stronger historical case for textual integrity and proximity to its claimed origin — and under which definitions?
meta.purpose: Debate-prep dossier: popular debates summarized, arguments steelmanned on both sides, academic receipts attached, opponent moves anticipated. No declared winner.
meta.warning: Clarify terms in the first 60 seconds. Most of this debate is lost on undefined words: historicity, preservation, inspiration, and 'corruption' are not synonyms.

definitions.precise: Whether the text we have can be traced, with historical methods, to a plausible origin event/community close to the claimed revelation or composition.
definitions.not: Not the same as 'true,' 'inspired,' or 'morally good.'

definitions.precise: Degree to which later copies match an earlier archetype (autograph or early fixed form). Measured by manuscripts, citations, and stemmatics.
definitions.not: Not proof of divine origin by itself.

definitions.precise: Theological claim that God authored or authorized the content.
definitions.not: Cannot be settled by carbon dating alone.

definitions.precise: Must specify: (a) wholesale textual rewrite, (b) interpretive distortion, (c) selective canon politics, or (d) ordinary scribal variation.
definitions.not: Do not let 'corruption' float as a vibe word.

definitions.precise: Authorized variant readings/modes in Islamic tradition. Debaters must say whether these count as 'different Qur'ans' or as licensed oral multiplicity inside one rasm.
definitions.not: Not automatically identical to NT manuscript variants.

definitions.precise: Consonantal skeleton of the Qur'anic text (pre-full vocalization/diacritics).
definitions.not: Not the same as a fully pointed modern printed mushaf.

debates.title: Is the New Testament We Possess Today Inspired?
debates.motion: Is the NT we possess today the inspired Word of God?
debates.summary: Ally uses critical NT scholarship (redaction, pseudonymity claims, variants) to deny that today's NT is fully inspired. White presses methodological consistency: if Ally's critical tools were applied to the Qur'an and Islamic tradition, Ally's own scripture claim collapses. Core clash: selective critical scholarship.

muslim: Appeal to Metzger-style textual criticism and liberal NT scholarship
Distinguish revealed kernel from human redaction in the Gospels
Argue inspiration claim fails for a text with unknown autographs and later changes
christian: Demand same critical standard for Qur'anic Jesus sayings and Islamic origins
Argue variants are known and do not erase reconstructability
Press the Islamic dilemma (Qur'an affirms prior scripture)

what_to_steal: Ask which scholars of the historical Jesus would endorse Qur'anic Jesus quotations

debates.title: Which is the Word of God — Bible or Qur'an?
debates.motion: Which is the Word of God: Bible or Qur'an?
debates.summary: Classic popular debate. Ally attacks NT authenticity via critical scholarship. Smith attacks Qur'anic historical foundations, manuscript late-control narratives, and presses Qur'anic affirmation of the Bible. Pattern still dominates street apologetics.

muslim: Manuscript differences and alleged embellishments in Gospels
Shift to moral/theological critique of OT law when pressed on Qur'an historicity
christian: Archaeology/manuscript comparison framing favoring Bible abundance
Qur'an affirms Bible; therefore Muslim corruption thesis is unstable
Challenge opponent to defend Qur'anic historical authenticity, not only attack Bible

what_to_steal: Don't spend the whole debate only attacking; defend your positive case
Watch for topic switch from historicity to ethics

debates.title: What Is the Qur'an's View of the Christian Scriptures?
debates.motion: What does the Qur'an teach about the Christian scriptures?
debates.summary: Focused Islamic-dilemma debate. Wood argues Qur'an affirms Torah/Gospel available to Jews/Christians; Ally argues affirmation is partial ('guidance and light therein') not wholesale endorsement of today's canon doctrines.

muslim: 5:47 means judge by what God revealed therein, not every later Christian claim
Qur'an knows and rejects Christian sonship claims (9:30)
Tahrif as misreading/concealment more than total textual annihilation
christian: 5:43–48; 10:94; 3:3–4 as affirmation of available scripture
Manuscript continuity from 7th c. to now blocks post-Muhammad corruption escape
Force binary: affirm Bible content or accuse Qur'an of error

what_to_steal: Distinguish textual continuity from doctrinal agreement

debates.title: The Preservation of the Bible and Qur'an
debates.motion: Comparative preservation of Bible and Qur'an
debates.summary: Direct preservation matchup. Green presses Qur'anic compilation reports, variant readings, and burning of materials. Kunde defends oral-written preservation model and attacks biblical textual instability.

muslim: Mass oral memorization as unique preservation mechanism
Uthmanic project as unification not invention
christian: Destruction of rival materials is a historical red flag
Qira'at and ahruf complicate letter-perfect claims
Transparent textual criticism is a strength, not a weakness

what_to_steal: Compare like with like: rasm vs autograph; Hafs print vs critical NT edition

debates.title: Qur'an or Bible: Which is the Word of God?
debates.motion: Which is the Word of God?
debates.summary: Broad Word-of-God debate. Hussain leans on critical biblical scholarship and Qur'anic preservation claims; Green emphasizes manuscript quantity and Qur'anic internal problems. Audience often treats 'Word of God' as historicity+theology fused — untangle that.

muslim: Challenge Christian overclaim from manuscript count alone
christian: Manuscript abundance and early citations
Hafs/Warsh and reading differences
Demand scholarly citations both ways

what_to_steal: Insist on academic sources, not just YouTube consensus

debates.title: Can We Trust the Text of the New Testament?
debates.motion: Can we trust the NT text / reconstruct the original?
debates.summary: Not Muslim-Christian, but the most important internal Christian/critical debate Muslims quote. Ehrman: early manuscript gap + massive variants → uncertainty. Wallace: abundance and earliness vs classical works → high reconstructability; most variants trivial; Ehrman's own books presuppose knowing the text.

christian: Embarrassment of riches vs Greco-Roman baseline
Early papyri + versions + fathers
Meaningful doctrinal variants are few and known

what_to_steal: If opponent cites Ehrman, ask if they accept Wallace's replies — and apply Ehrman-level skepticism to Islamic sources
Never let '400,000 variants' stand without explaining how variants are counted

debates.title: Yasir Qadhi: 'The standard narrative has holes in it'
debates.summary: Qadhi acknowledged that popular preservation storytelling cannot handle ahruf/qira'at complexities; advanced scholars struggle with unanswered questions. Christian apologists weaponized this; traditional Muslims accused him of overstatement or dangerous theory.

internal-muslim: Distinguish academic complexity from denial of preservation
Ahruf as divine concession / multiple modes
Reject letter-for-letter folk claim without rejecting wahy
critics: If narrative has holes, perfect-preservation slogan fails
Qira'at meaning differences are not zero
Use admission as peer testimony against street apologetics

what_to_steal: Quote carefully: Qadhi did not say 'Qur'an is corrupted' in the Christian sense
Ask opponent which preservation claim they actually make: rasm? Hafs? all ten qira'at?

links.label: Traditionalist critique of Qadhi ahruf theory

debates.title: White/Ally extended consistency war (redaction criticism)
debates.motion: May one use liberal critical tools on the Bible while shielding the Qur'an?
debates.summary: Long-running meta-debate. White: Ally cites Dunn/Brown/Metzger against Bible but would reject their verdict that Qur'anic Jesus material is historically worthless. Ally: Qur'an is a different genre/claim and does not endorse every Gospel sentence.

muslim: Critical tools diagnose human texts; Qur'an is guarded revelation
christian: Special pleading
Cradle speech of Jesus / Infancy Gospel parallels as consistency test

what_to_steal: Prepare a 30-second 'method symmetry' speech and reuse it

arguments.title: Definition trap: historicity vs preservation vs inspiration

bible_case.claim: If historicity means recoverability of an early text and proximity to events, the Bible's multi-witness manuscript tradition and early citations are a strength.
bible_case.case: Christian debaters often win when the motion is 'can we know approximately what was written?' and lose when they overclaim 'letter inspiration of the KJV/TR' or ignore OT textual plurality.

sources.label: Metzger & Ehrman, The Text of the New Testament

quran_case.claim: If historicity means early fixation of a controlled text tied to a single revelatory event in one lifetime, the Qur'an's short revelation window + early rasm + oral culture is stronger.
quran_case.case: Muslim debaters often win when the motion is 'which book was standardized earlier relative to its prophet?' and lose when they claim zero meaningful variation or deny manuscript complexity.

arguments.counter_to_bible: Manuscript count ≠ autographic certainty; OT/NT are different problems bundled unfairly.
arguments.counter_to_quran: Early standardization can coexist with suppressed alternatives (companion codices, Sanaa C-1).
arguments.crux: What exact question is being debated tonight — and which metric wins?
arguments.debate_use: Open with this. If you lose definitions, you lose.

arguments.title: New Testament variants and reconstructability

bible_case.claim: Despite hundreds of thousands of variants, the NT text is reconstructable with high confidence for nearly all passages; meaningful uncertain cases are known and published.
bible_case.case: Wallace et al.: quantity + relatively early witnesses beat classical baseline. Most variants are spelling/word order. Critical editions (NA/UBS) document uncertainty. Ehrman's popular rhetoric often outruns his technical practice.

quran_case.claim: The scale of NT variation and centuries of copying before abundant manuscripts undercut claims of a stable inspired text comparable to the Qur'an.
quran_case.case: Muslim apologetics cite Ehrman, Metzger's catalogues of variants, longer ending of Mark, Pericope Adulterae, Comma Johanneum. Argument: if Christians needed centuries of criticism to approximate an original, 'Bible historicity' is overstated.

sources.label: Ally/White debate use of critical scholarship

arguments.counter_to_bible: Early gap (1st–2nd c.) still matters; some variants are theologically loaded.
arguments.counter_to_quran: Citing Ehrman against Bible while rejecting his historical Jesus conclusions is cherry-picking.
arguments.crux: Are we measuring 'number of differences' or 'ability to recover an early text'?
arguments.debate_use: Have 3 showcase variants ready (Mark 16; John 7:53–8:11; 1 John 5:7) and what critical text does with them.

arguments.title: Old Testament: MT, LXX, Dead Sea Scrolls

bible_case.claim: Dead Sea Scrolls show substantial continuity of Hebrew Bible traditions centuries before Islam; plurality of text-types is real but bounded and studyable.
bible_case.case: DSS sometimes confirm MT, sometimes support LXX-like readings. This is controlled textual history, not free invention. Emanuel Tov's work is the academic baseline.

sources.label: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible

quran_case.claim: OT textual plurality (MT/LXX/SP/DSS) and late medieval MT exemplars show the Hebrew Bible was not preserved as a single fixed text.
quran_case.case: Muslim debaters note Leningrad/Aleppo are medieval; Samaritan Pentateuch diverges; some books (Jeremiah) have major literary editions. Compared with Uthmanic rasm unity, Bible looks fluid.

sources.label: Tov on LXX in biblical research

arguments.counter_to_bible: Don't pretend one OT text-type always wins; be honest about Jeremiah/Samuel issues.
arguments.counter_to_quran: Literary editions ≠ 'Bible invented in Middle Ages'; DSS smash that slogan.
arguments.crux: Is textual plurality evidence of corruption or of a normal ancient textual culture?
arguments.debate_use: Bring one DSS example that confirms MT and one that supports LXX — shows literacy, not panic.

arguments.title: Uthmanic standardization and rasm unity

bible_case.claim: Caliphal standardization + destruction of rival materials is the opposite of transparent preservation; it is state canon control.
bible_case.case: Bukhari 4987 is used constantly: Uthman orders copies, burns others. Christian debaters argue this hides the evidence trail the Bible still exposes through competing manuscripts.

quran_case.claim: Uthmanic project preserved a Prophetic/early archetype already widely known; burning prevented regional conflict over secondary differences, not invention of a new book.
quran_case.case: van Putten: shared orthographic idiosyncrasies across manuscripts indicate a single written archetype. Sadeghi: among early text-types, Uthmanic appears closest to prototype. Oral mutawatir + written rasm = dual preservation.

arguments.counter_to_bible: Bible also had canon politics (and book-burning episodes in Christian history).
arguments.counter_to_quran: If alternatives were burned, empirical comparison is partly destroyed by design.
arguments.crux: Was Uthman transmitting a fixed revelation or selecting among living textual options?
arguments.debate_use: Concede companion differences existed; fight over whether they threaten Prophetic origin.

arguments.title: Sanaa palimpsest (C-1) and companion codices

bible_case.claim: Sanaa lower text proves a non-Uthmanic Qur'anic text-type existed — so 'one unchanged Qur'an from the beginning' is false.
bible_case.case: Lower text shows word/phrase substitutions, omissions/additions, some sura-order issues in broader companion reports. Used to parallel Bible textual plurality.

sources.label: JAOS review essay Beyond the Cairo Edition

quran_case.claim: C-1 is a companion-codex style secondary text-type; stemmatics indicate Uthmanic is older/closer to Prophetic prototype, so Sanaa confirms early multiplicity of hearing/writing, not late fabrication.
quran_case.case: Sadeghi & Bergmann: polarity analysis favors Uthmanic wording as earlier; prototype identified with Prophetic recension. Upper text is standard. Thus manuscript age + divergence can support early origin rather than undermine it.

arguments.counter_to_bible: One divergent palimpsest is not 'thousands of Qur'ans.'
arguments.counter_to_quran: If companion codices differed in wording, 'verbatim identity' slogans fail.
arguments.crux: Does C-1 refute Prophetic origin, or only refute a folk model of clone-identical first copies?
arguments.debate_use: Memorize both uses of Sanaa: attack folk Islam / defend early origin. Pick based on your thesis.

arguments.title: Birmingham folios and radiocarbon dating

bible_case.claim: C-14 dates parchment, not ink; paleography may place writing later; early date ranges can even tension Uthmanic chronology depending on interpretation.
bible_case.case: Academic caution (Reynolds et al.): media overclaimed 'oldest Qur'an.' Dating must combine C-14 with paleography/orthography. Not a knock-out for either side alone.

quran_case.claim: Early parchment dates (568–645 CE range) place Qur'anic text remarkably close to Muhammad's lifetime, supporting rapid writing and stability.
quran_case.case: Islamic Awareness and Muslim apologetics use Birmingham + other C-14 results to argue the Qur'an is among the best-attested late antique scriptures in chronological proximity.

arguments.counter_to_bible: Even with caution, early dates are impressive compared with many biblical autograph gaps.
arguments.counter_to_quran: Parchment reuse / pre-slaughter animal age means C-14 is a terminus post quem soft bound.
arguments.crux: What does C-14 actually date — and what claim is being smuggled from that date?
arguments.debate_use: Never let a C-14 slide stand without asking: parchment or ink? range or point estimate?

arguments.title: Ahruf, qira'at, and 'perfect preservation'

bible_case.claim: Multiple canonical readings with occasional meaning differences falsify street-level 'every letter identical' preservation.
bible_case.case: Examples like siḥrān/sāḥirān type differences are used rhetorically. Qadhi's 'holes' line is treated as concession. Argument: if ten readings are all Qur'an, then 'one text' needs redefinition.

quran_case.claim: Qira'at are authorized oral manifestations within an Uthmanic rasm; preservation includes licensed multiplicity, not a modern printer's identical-PDF expectation.
quran_case.case: Classical ulum al-Qur'an literature long discussed seven ahruf. Modern academic work treats canonical readings as a reading tradition family, not random corruption. Folk overclaim is the problem.

sources.label: van Putten research program on readings/rasm

arguments.counter_to_bible: NT 'critical text' also chooses among readings; Christians live with plurality too.
arguments.counter_to_quran: If meanings differ, divine dictation models must explain why.
arguments.crux: Is preservation identity of letters, identity of rasm, or identity of authorized reading corpus?
arguments.debate_use: Force opponent to state their preservation thesis in one sentence before you answer.

arguments.title: Scribal corrections in early Qur'an manuscripts (Brubaker debate)

bible_case.claim: Physical corrections show the text was altered toward a later standard — evidence of fluidity.
bible_case.case: Brubaker's Corrections in Early Qurʾān Manuscripts popularized images of insertions/erasures. Apologists infer doctrinal/editorial drift before Cairo 1924 stabilization around Hafs.

quran_case.claim: Corrections are ordinary scribal error fixes aligning copies to an already known text; Brubaker overinterprets methodologically.
quran_case.case: Hythem Sidky's review: bold claims unsubstantiated; most examples best explained as scribal error first. Altıkulaç/IRCICA refutation from Muslim manuscript scholarship. Presence of uncorrected early witnesses matching rasm undermines 'late creation' inference.

arguments.counter_to_bible: NT manuscripts are full of corrections too; that is how hand-copying works.
arguments.counter_to_quran: Patterns of correction still deserve stemmatic study; dismissiveness is not a method.
arguments.crux: Do corrections converge on an early archetype or manufacture a later one?
arguments.debate_use: If opponent shows a photo of an erasure, ask for the control: uncorrected early parallels.

arguments.title: Islamic dilemma: Qur'an affirms prior scripture

bible_case.claim: Qur'an tells People of the Gospel to judge by what they have; 7th-c. Bible ≈ today's in core; therefore Islam affirms a Bible that contradicts Islam — dilemma.
bible_case.case: 5:47, 5:68, 10:94, 3:3–4. Continuity of manuscripts across Muhammad's time is the historical lever.

quran_case.claim: Affirmation is of revelation/guidance within prior books, not of every Christian doctrine; Qur'an is muhaymin and corrects; tahrif primarily targets misuse/concealment.
quran_case.case: Abdullah Saeed: Qur'an reveres Tawrat/Injil while criticizing people. Ally: 'contains guidance and light' ≠ 'is entirely guidance and light.'

arguments.counter_to_bible: If 'Gospel' means a book given to Jesus, four Gospels are already a category mismatch.
arguments.counter_to_quran: If the available Injil in 7th c. taught crucifixion/deity, partial-affirmation still collides.
arguments.crux: What object does 'Injil' refer to in Q 5 — and what propositional content is affirmed?
arguments.debate_use: This is often the Christian best offensive tool; prepare the precise Ally/Saeed reply.

arguments.title: Method symmetry (critical tools both ways)

bible_case.claim: If form/redaction criticism can dissolve Gospel historicity, the same toolkit dissolves sira/hadith and treats Qur'anic Jesus material as late non-historical.
bible_case.case: White's consistency challenge: scholars Ally cites would not validate cradle speech of Jesus in the Qur'an. You cannot borrow their sword and forbid them to swing it at Islam.

quran_case.claim: The Qur'an's claim-structure differs: single revelatory book in one language vs multi-author library; applying identical tools ignores genre and transmission model differences.
quran_case.case: Muslim reply: historical-critical method developed inside biblical studies; Islamic sciences have isnad/hadith criticism. Also: even critical scholars often affirm early Qur'anic rasm fixation.

arguments.counter_to_bible: Difference of genre is real; not every biblical tool maps 1:1.
arguments.counter_to_quran: If you use Metzger against Mark, you need a principled reason not to use Déroche/van Putten critically.
arguments.crux: What is the shared historical method both sides accept before theology?
arguments.debate_use: Best 'judo' move in the entire topic. Practice a 45-second version.

arguments.title: Authorship and dating of composition

bible_case.claim: Multiple attestation and early creedal material (e.g. 1 Cor 15) give historical traction to core events even if some books' traditional authorship is debated.
bible_case.case: Split the question: (1) who wrote Hebrews? vs (2) was Jesus crucified under Pilate?

quran_case.claim: Qur'an originates in a single prophetic career (c. 610–632) with early community memory; Bible spans centuries with anonymous/pseudonymous parts.
quran_case.case: Shorter revelation window is offered as historicity advantage for the Qur'an as a book.

arguments.counter_to_bible: Critical dating of Gospels decades later still beats 600+ year gap for Jesus material in Qur'an.
arguments.counter_to_quran: Sira/hadith historicization is itself critically contested (Donner etc.).
arguments.crux: Are we dating the book as artifact, or the events the book narrates?
arguments.debate_use: Split 'book historicity' from 'event historicity' on the whiteboard.

arguments.title: Book reliability vs event reliability (Jesus as test case)

bible_case.claim: On the historical Jesus, mainstream scholarship aligns more with crucifixion than with Qur'anic denial — so Bible-related sources win the event test even if textual variants exist.
bible_case.case: Craig/Ehrman agree on crucifixion facticity; Qur'an 4:157 is the collision point.

quran_case.claim: Event claims in revelation are not hostage to Roman historians; also 4:157 can be read as denying agency/boast, and later tafsir is not identical to the verse.
quran_case.case: Lawson/Isma'ili/academic minority readings; theological epistemology vs positivist history.

arguments.counter_to_bible: Historical consensus ≠ infallible; ancient consensus can be wrong.
arguments.counter_to_quran: If you enter a 'historicity' debate, positivist historical method is the agreed arena.
arguments.crux: Is tonight's standard public historical method, or revelatory authority?
arguments.debate_use: If motion says 'historicity,' pin the standard to public history early.

opponent_cards.fast_answer: Variants are counted per manuscript difference, not 400k alternate Bibles. Most are spelling. Ask which variant changes a doctrine and whether critical editions flag it.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Then apply the same numeric scare to qira'at/manuscript corrections.

opponent_cards.trigger: The Qur'an is perfectly preserved letter for letter
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Ask: Hafs only? all ten? rasm only? Companion codices? Sanaa C-1? Qadhi himself said the standard narrative has holes regarding ahruf/qira'at.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Offer a precise alternative: early Uthmanic rasm is remarkably stable — without folk overclaim.

opponent_cards.trigger: Uthman burned the evidence, so the Qur'an is unreliable
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Burning explains conflict control; it does not by itself prove invention. Stemmatic/orthographic work argues a single archetype. But it does undercut 'we can empirically inspect all rivals.'
opponent_cards.follow_up: Demand consistency about Christian canon politics.

opponent_cards.trigger: Ehrman proved the Bible is corrupted
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Ehrman argues uncertainty and early gap; he still reconstructs texts and affirms crucifixion. If you trust Ehrman against Bible inspiration, do you trust him against Qur'anic Jesus history?
sources: Misquoting Jesus vs his academic editions

opponent_cards.trigger: Birmingham manuscript proves the Qur'an is unchanged
opponent_cards.fast_answer: It dates parchment to a range, not ink to a day, and covers limited folios. Strong evidence of early writing; not a total proof of global letter-identity.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Affirm what's fair: proximity to origin is impressive.

opponent_cards.trigger: Sanaa proves the Qur'an was rewritten
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Sanaa lower text is a non-Uthmanic type. Sadeghi argues Uthmanic is closer to prototype. It challenges clone-identical folk history more than Prophetic origin as such.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask opponent if they have read Sadeghi/Hilali or only apologetics clips.

opponent_cards.trigger: The Qur'an confirms the Bible, so Muslims must accept the Gospels
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Define Injil. Ally/Saeed: contains guidance/light; judge by what God revealed therein; Qur'an simultaneously rejects sonship. Affirmation ≠ blank check.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Then fight the historical content question separately (crucifixion).

opponent_cards.trigger: Dead Sea Scrolls prove the OT is unchanged
opponent_cards.fast_answer: DSS prove early Hebrew traditions and much continuity, also real plurality (MT/LXX-like). Good against 'medieval invention'; not proof of zero variation.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Keep OT and NT arguments unbundled.

opponent_cards.fast_answer: Photos show corrections. Sidky: usually scribal error fixes; bold corruption thesis not shown. Hand-copied Bibles look the same under a lens.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask for a variant that cannot be explained as dittography/haplography/alignment to known rasm.

opponent_cards.trigger: Only the Qur'an was memorized by thousands
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Oral frequency matters, but memory preserves what communities standardize; it can also stabilize a chosen reading. Pair oral claims with manuscript stemmata.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask how oral model handles documented companion differences.

prep_checklist: Write your one-sentence motion interpretation and get agreement at the start
Prepare a 60-second definitions opener (historicity / preservation / inspiration / tahrif)
Choose a positive case (not only attack): 3 pillars max
Master 5 receipts you can cite cold (2 Bible, 2 Qur'an, 1 method)
Drill the 10 opponent cards out loud
Watch/listen: Wallace–Ehrman 2011; one Ally–White; one Ally–Wood dilemma debate
Read: Sadeghi & Bergmann abstract+conclusion; van Putten 2019; Saeed on tahrif; Wallace variant FAQ
Decide in advance what you will grant if pressed on Sanaa / qira'at / Mark 16
Prepare closing: restate crux questions, not slogans
Bring printed primary quotes (Bukhari 4987; Q 5:47; Ehrman crucifixion line; van Putten thesis sentence)

if_defending_bible_historicity: Public historical method reconstructs NT text better than classical analogs (Wallace line)
DSS/LXX/MT give the Hebrew Bible a real Second Temple footprint
On Jesus events, critical consensus favors crucifixion over Qur'anic denial
if_defending_quran_historicity: Short revelatory window + early rasm archetype (van Putten/Sadeghi)
Oral-written dual transmission unique in scale
Companion variants/Sanaa show early textual ecology, not 8th-c. fabrication from nothing
C-14 early parchments support proximity to origin
if_seeking_unity_steelman: Both scriptures have serious historical footprints; folk slogans on both sides are the enemy
Agree on shared vocabulary before theology
Separate book-as-artifact questions from salvation claims
Use academic literature both sides actually respect
